t: #2645 Minimum Additions to Make Valid String
o: A valid string is repetitions of "abc". Scan word while tracking the expected next character of the current abc block. When word's character differs from expected, we must insert the missing characters between them: (expected - actual) mod 3 insertions, then the actual character advances the expectation. After consuming word, finish the trailing partial block with ('c' - expected) mod 3 more insertions. E.g. "b": expect 'a', mismatch costs 1, then finish with 'c' costing 1 → 2. "aaa": each 'a' forces inserting 'b','c' → 6.
k: Track expected character cycling a→b→c; a mismatch of gap d requires d insertions.
After the scan, close out the partial block with the remaining characters.
Greedy insertion is optimal because insertions are forced by the fixed abc pattern.

a.i: Walk the string maintaining the expected letter; each mismatch contributes (expected - seen + 3) % 3 insertions, then resync.
s: For each character c: add (expected - c + 3) % 3 to the answer; set expected to the successor of c in the cycle a→b→c→a.

a.n: Approach 2: Count 'abc' Blocks via Pattern Removal
a.i: Every maximal occurrence structure corresponds to blocks; equivalently, count how many times 'abc' appears as a subsequence-aligned unit and derive additions as 3*blocks - adjustments. A cleaner variant: repeatedly find and remove "abc" substrings; insertions = 3*(number of blocks) - remaining length logic. Practically, a stack-based simulation inserting missing letters yields the same count.
s: Use a stack; push characters of word.
Whenever top three form 'a','b','c', pop them and increment blocks.
Additions = 3 * blocks_needed - len(word), where blocks_needed is derived by simulating insertions greedily.
a.t: O(n) — single pass with constant work per character

w: Both approaches are the same greedy in different clothes; Approach 1 is the tightest. Pitfall: the modulo direction — (cur - exp + 3) % 3 counts how many letters precede c in the cycle. Follow-up: generalize to concatenations of an arbitrary pattern p (track expected index mod |p|).
